newsitem.title: USA: Indiana corn, soy harvests aided by ideal weather.
newsitem.headline: Indiana corn, soy harvests aided by ideal weather.

text.p: Indiana corn and soybean harvests were boosted by ideal weather while the condition of both crops improved in the week to Sunday, said the state's Agricultural Statistics Service in its weekly report.
"Early reports indicated minimal damage to crops from the first frost which occurred last week," it added.
Corn was rated 45 percent good to excellent, up from 44 percent a week ago. Corn was eight percent harvested, versus 32 percent last year and a five-year average of 26 percent.
Seventy percent of corn acreage was mature, versus 97 percent last year and an average of 91 percent.
Soybeans were rated 41 percent good to excellent, up from 40 percent a week earlier.

Twelve percent of soybeans had been harvested, compared with 52 percent last year and an average of 42 percent. Forty-eight percent of soybeans were mature, versus 88 percent last year and an average of 86 percent.
Winter wheat was 14 percent planted, down from both the five-year average and last year's 29 percent.
Topsoil moisture was rated six percent surplus, 77 percent adequate, 15 percent short and two percent very short.
